_README: PROPOSED permission overlay for unattended agent work. NOT ACTIVE.
REWRITTEN 2026-09-10. The previous version of this block said the order path
'stays behind .claude/hooks/guard_order_path.py'. That file was deleted the
same day (7ad3a82, on the team lead's instruction, together with its tests),
and so was apply_autonomy.py, which this block told you to run. THERE IS NO
PreToolUse HOOK IN THIS REPO. .claude/README.md:28 says so plainly, and this
file contradicted it.
That is not a documentation slip. This overlay allows `Bash(python3 *)`, and
the live session entry point, the MOC routing probe, reset_epoch,
switch_broker and cancel_open_orders are all `python3 ...` commands. Applied
as it stood, with the hook gone, it granted silent unattended access to every
irreversible action in the repo while its own README promised the opposite.
HOW TO APPLY IT NOW. apply_autonomy.py no longer exists. Paste the
`permissions` block into .claude/settings.json yourself, or add the entries
through /permissions.
WHAT IT DOES. Removes the friction from everything reversible -- running any
research script, any test, any analysis, editing any file outside the frozen
specs, fetching from the primary sources this desk actually cites -- so a
session can work all night without stopping for approvals.
WHAT NOW HOLDS THE ORDER PATH. The `deny` list below, and nothing else.
Deny beats allow in Claude Code's permission model, so these entries survive
the broad `Bash(python3 *)` above. They are a REPLACEMENT FOR THE HOOK AND
THEY ARE WEAKER THAN IT WAS: they match on the command string, so an
equivalent command written another way -- a `cd` first, a shell variable, a
wrapper script, a different interpreter -- is not matched. Treat them as a
guardrail against the obvious mistake, NOT as a sandbox, and do not let their
presence talk you into a broader allow list than you would otherwise write.
WHY THESE ACTIONS AND NOT OTHERS. Each one cannot be undone. An NYSE MOC
cannot be cancelled after 15:50 ET, not even to correct a legitimate error.
The trade phase is not idempotent and there is no dedupe at the broker, so a
second armed run stacks a second order set and both fill in the same auction.
A fill not captured before the daily TWS restart is gone permanently.
promote.sh checks out a different tag over the live tree.
TO RESTORE THE REAL GUARD instead, which is stronger than any deny list:
git show 7ad3a82^:.claude/hooks/guard_order_path.py > .claude/hooks/guard_order_path.py
git show 7ad3a82^:.claude/hooks/tests/test_guard_order_path.py > .claude/hooks/tests/test_guard_order_path.py
chmod +x .claude/hooks/guard_order_path.py
# then re-add the PreToolUse block to .claude/settings.json
It was removed deliberately; restoring it is the team lead's call, not an
agent's. Until then the standing arrangement is the one CLAUDE.md describes:
the agent proposes the command and a human runs it with `! <command>`.
_deny_notes: The Bash entries in `deny` replace the deleted PreToolUse hook and are
command-STRING matches only: an equivalent command written another way (a
`cd` first, a shell variable, a wrapper, a different interpreter) is not
matched. A guardrail against the obvious mistake, not a sandbox.
The Read/Edit entries are the credential rule: never print, copy or
transmit one. To test whether a key is set, print the boolean, never the
_ask_notes: These open a broker socket but transmit no order (preflight, capture_fills
and reconcile_orders connect readonly). They are `ask` rather than `allow`
because a socket to the live account is worth a human glance, and rather
than `deny` because refusing them would stop the reversible diagnosis work
that a stuck session most needs.
